newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel approves Barshefsky for trade post.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel approves Barshefsky for trade post.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Finance Committee on Thursday voted to recommend Charlene Barshefsky for the position of U.S. Trade Representative and to remove a legal barrier so she can take that job.

The panel voted in favour of a waiver of a 1995 law that prevents those who have worked for foreign governments from holding the post. As a private attorney, Barshefsky advised Canada in 1990 on a lumber dispute with the United States.
The vote was unanimous among the committee senators who were present and followed a confirmation hearing on Wednesday.
The full Senate must vote on the nomination for Barshefsky to be confirmed. Both the House of Representatives and the Senate must approve the waiver.
President Bill Clinton nominated Barshefsky to the position. She has been the acting top U.S. trade negotiator since last April, when she succeeded Mickey Kantor.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he remained concerned about the waiver.

"I don't think you can lightly dismiss a law that's on the books," Lott said. The Mississippi Republican said he would continue to emphasise that the law was there for a reason and that he was continuing to review the issue.
It was unclear when the full Senate would take up Barshefsky's nomination. The House was expected to wait for Senate action on the waiver before considering it.

"When you have been a representative of foreign countries, for you then to come in the door on the other side as the United States trade representative, we need to think about that very carefully," Lott said.
"I'm going to talk to our counsels, our lawyers on it, and we'll make a decision on that in another couple of weeks probably," he added.
